title: Payment Processing & Ledger
summary: Authorize, capture, refund, and reconcile merchant payments without double-charging or losing money.
statement:
Design a multi-tenant payment processing platform that lets online merchants charge buyers across card networks and regional payment providers, record an auditable financial ledger, and reconcile daily settlements.

Functional requirements:
- Expose merchant APIs to authorize, capture, void, and refund payments using integer minor currency units.
- Guarantee that client or gateway retries never double-charge a buyer, even when external payment providers time out mid-request.
- Maintain an immutable financial ledger for merchant balances, platform fees, and refunds.
- Deliver signed payment-status webhooks to merchants and reconcile internal records against daily provider settlement files.

Scale to assume:
- 250,000 active merchants processing 40 million payment transactions per day.
- Peak checkout traffic of 5,000 payment mutations per second and 25,000 status reads per second.
- External card networks and payment providers have p99 latency of 1 to 4 seconds and experience intermittent timeouts and duplicate callbacks.
hints: Never hold a database transaction or row lock open across a 2-second external provider call. Break checkout into durable state transitions around the network boundary.
A timeout from an external payment provider means `UNKNOWN`, not `FAILED`. How should your attempt state machine, provider idempotency key, and recovery worker handle an ambiguous response?
Mutable `balance = balance - amount` columns make audits and discrepancy debugging painful. Model money movement as balanced, append-only ledger entries paired with an outbox for webhooks.
expectations: Clarifies currency representation (integer minor units + ISO currency code, never floating point), PCI token boundary (vaulted payment-method tokens rather than raw PANs), and separate authorize vs capture flows.
Enforces `(merchant_id, idempotency_key)` uniqueness with a canonical request-payload hash so identical retries replay the stored outcome while mutated payloads under the same key are rejected.
Models explicit `PaymentIntent` and `PaymentAttempt` state machines (`CREATED`, `AUTHORIZING`, `AUTHORIZED`, `CAPTURING`, `CAPTURED`, `FAILED`, `UNKNOWN`) guarded by conditional versioned updates.
Commits intent/attempt state before calling external payment providers so no database transaction or connection stays open across slow third-party RPCs.
Treats provider timeouts and 5xx responses as `UNKNOWN`, reconciling status via provider-side idempotency keys, status queries, or webhooks before ever issuing a new charge attempt.

Records money movement in an append-only, balanced double-entry ledger (buyer clearing, merchant payable, platform fee, refund entries) and emits signed, deduplicated merchant webhooks via a transactional outbox.
Runs an asynchronous settlement reconciliation pipeline against daily PSP/bank files to surface missing, mismatched, or late-settled transactions for operational resolution.
